title: First starter skill evaluation
modelSetup: Fresh Codex subagents inheriting the same session configuration. Exact backend model identifier was not exposed; no model override was used.
grading: Two separate fresh Codex graders scored three cases each with A/B condition labels hidden. The coordinator then inspected all 12 outputs and the grading. No human validation has been performed.
findings: The with-skill outputs met 30 of 30 predefined checks; baseline outputs met 28 of 30.

Both missed baseline checks concern the same no-candidate case: it offered no concrete recurring-work follow-up. These two checks overlap, so the gap should not be interpreted as two independent improvements.
Both conditions met every check in the other five cases; these fixtures show little incremental benefit over this baseline.
The with-skill outputs were longer in all six cases.

A with-skill Daily Debrief output incorrectly counted six excerpts as seven. This factual error was outside the original rubric, showing that a full rubric score does not mean an output is error-free.
limitations: Six hand-authored fictional cases, not workplace outcome data.
One execution per case and condition; no uncertainty interval or significance claim.
Same inherited model configuration for execution and grading; exact backend identifier unavailable.
Only two starter skills tested; the other four have not had behavioral evaluations.
Explicit skill loading; installation, automatic triggering, MCP integrations, scheduling, multi-model portability, latency and cost were not tested.
Rubric was frozen before output inspection, while execution was in progress; one wording typo was clarified before grading.
Model-generated grading with coordinator AI review; no human scoring.
Pass counts measure the stated checks, not real-world productivity, accuracy or hours saved.
wordCountMethod: Regex word-like sequences in raw Markdown, including source IDs and structured records; this is a reproducible length measure, not a readability score. Informal counts in raw grader notes are unverified estimates and can differ; the recomputation script defines the published counts.
nextSteps: Shorten the default answer, retaining detailed continuity records only when useful.
Replace overlapping no-candidate criteria with distinct task outcomes and add a factual-count check.
Repeat across more cases and explicitly identified models, and invite human review.
